content:
Overview

The Free Drugs Service Initiative is a component of the National Health Mission (NHM) that ensures free essential medicines to patients visiting public health facilities. Under the initiative, state governments receive financial support to strengthen drug procurement, storage, and distribution systems, and to maintain an assured supply of essential medicines at primary health centres, community health centres, and district hospitals. The goal is to reduce out of pocket expenditure on medicines for patients.

Eligibility Criteria

  • All patients availing treatment at government health facilities are eligible
  • Free medicines are provided during outpatient and inpatient treatment
  • No income or category restrictions apply

Benefits

  • Free essential medicines at public health facilities as per the state's essential drug list
  • Reduction in out of pocket healthcare expenses for families
  • Improved drug availability through better procurement and supply chain systems
  • Special provision of medicines for chronic conditions such as diabetes and hypertension at many facilities

How to Apply

  1. Visit the nearest government health facility for consultation
  2. Register at the outpatient counter and get a prescription from the doctor
  3. Collect the prescribed medicines free of cost from the facility's pharmacy

Required Documents

  • Aadhaar card or any government-issued identity proof
  • Prescription from the treating doctor
meta_title: Free Drugs Service Initiative: Free Medicines at Govt Hospitals
meta_description: The Free Drugs Service Initiative under NHM provides free essential medicines to patients at government health facilities. Check eligibility and how it works.

content:
Overview

PM Kisan Maandhan Yojana is a voluntary pension scheme for small and marginal farmers in India, launched by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare. The scheme provides a monthly pension of Rs 3,000 to farmers aged 60 years and above. Farmers between 18 and 40 years of age can enrol by contributing a small monthly amount, which is matched by an equal contribution from the central government. The scheme complements the PM Kisan Samman Nidhi income support programme.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Small and marginal farmers with up to 2 hectares of cultivable land
  • Age between 18 and 40 years at the time of enrolment
  • Not covered under other social security schemes such as EPFO, ESIC, or NPS
  • Not an income tax payer

Benefits

  • Assured monthly pension of Rs 3,000 after reaching 60 years of age
  • Equal contribution from the central government to the farmer's pension account
  • Family pension of 50 percent of the monthly amount to the spouse after the farmer's demise
  • Enrolment through a simple monthly contribution starting from Rs 55 for the youngest entrants

How to Apply

  1. Visit the nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) with the required documents
  2. Fill the enrolment form with your land and bank details
  3. Submit the form and start paying the monthly contribution
  4. Contributions can also be made through the PM Kisan Maandhan web portal

Required Documents

  • Aadhaar card
  • Bank account details with IFSC code
  • Land records or a self declaration of landholding
  • Mobile number linked to Aadhaar
meta_title: PM Kisan Maandhan Yojana: Pension of Rs 3,000 for Farmers
meta_description: PM Kisan Maandhan provides Rs 3,000 monthly pension to small and marginal farmers at age 60. Check eligibility, monthly contribution, and how to apply.

content:
Overview

e-NAM, the electronic National Agriculture Market, is a pan-India online trading platform launched by the Government of India to create a unified national market for agricultural produce. The platform connects mandis, farmers, traders, and buyers, allowing transparent price discovery and online bidding for farm produce. Farmers can list their produce online and compare prices across mandis before selling, leading to better returns.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Farmers registered with mandis on the e-NAM platform can trade online
  • Traders, commission agents, and buyers need registration on the platform
  • Farmer producer organisations and bulk buyers can also register

Benefits

  • Transparent online bidding and price discovery across more than 1,300 mandis
  • Better price realisation by selling to buyers beyond the local mandi
  • Single window for payments directly to the farmer's bank account
  • Reduced intermediary costs and faster settlement of transactions

How to Apply

  1. Register on the e-NAM portal using your Aadhaar and bank details
  2. Get your produce quality assessed at the mandi
  3. List the produce for online bidding and accept the best bid
  4. Receive payment directly in your bank account after delivery

Required Documents

  • Aadhaar card
  • Bank account details
  • Identity proof and mandi registration details
meta_title: e-NAM: Online Agricultural Market for Better Farmer Prices
meta_description: e-NAM connects farmers to a national online marketplace for transparent bidding and better prices. Learn how to register and trade on the platform.

content:
Overview

Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) is a sub-mission of the National Mission on Natural Farming that promotes organic farming in India. Under the scheme, farmers are organised into clusters to adopt certified organic cultivation methods, free from chemical fertilisers and pesticides. The scheme provides financial assistance for organic inputs, certification, and marketing, and encourages traditional, natural, and regenerative farming practices.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Individual farmers and groups of farmers willing to adopt organic farming
  • Farmer clusters formed with a minimum area, typically 50 acres, in a village or contiguous area
  • Existing conventional farmers converting to organic methods are prioritised

Benefits

  • Financial assistance of Rs 50,000 per hectare over three years for organic inputs and activities
  • Support for organic certification and participation in local organic markets
  • Assistance for value addition, packaging, and marketing of organic produce
  • Better premium prices for certified organic produce

How to Apply

  1. Contact the agriculture department of your district or the nodal agency for PKVY
  2. Form a farmer cluster and submit the cluster proposal
  3. Undergo training on organic practices and receive input assistance
  4. Complete certification and market the produce through supported channels

Required Documents

  • Land records
  • Aadhaar card and bank account details
  • Cluster formation details and farmer consent
meta_title: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana: Organic Farming Assistance
meta_description: PKVY promotes certified organic farming with Rs 50,000 per hectare assistance over three years. Know cluster formation, eligibility, and benefits.

content:
Overview

Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) is a flagship scheme of the Government of India with the motto Har Khet Ko Pani, meaning water for every field. The scheme aims to extend irrigation coverage, improve water use efficiency, and promote precision irrigation through micro-irrigation systems. It integrates multiple ongoing irrigation programmes under one umbrella and focuses on end to end water management from source to farm.

Eligibility Criteria

  • All farmers with cultivable land are eligible for assistance under the scheme
  • Priority for small and marginal farmers and farmers in water scarce regions
  • Individual farmers and farmer groups can avail micro-irrigation subsidies

Benefits

  • Subsidy support for drip and sprinkler irrigation systems, typically up to 55 percent for small and marginal farmers
  • Creation of new irrigation infrastructure and repair of existing water bodies
  • Per drop more crop through improved water use efficiency
  • Support for rainwater harvesting and watershed development

How to Apply

  1. Visit the district agriculture office or the state agriculture department portal
  2. Submit the application for micro-irrigation assistance with land details
  3. Get the proposal approved and install the irrigation system through empanelled suppliers
  4. Claim the subsidy through the designated process after verification

Required Documents

  • Land ownership or tenancy records
  • Aadhaar card and bank account details
  • Quotation from empanelled micro-irrigation supplier
meta_title: PM Krishi Sinchayee Yojana: Irrigation Subsidy for Farmers
meta_description: PMKSY aims Har Khet Ko Pani with subsidies for drip and sprinkler irrigation. Check eligibility, subsidy rates, and how to apply for irrigation support.

content:
Overview

The National Food Security Mission (NFSM) is a centrally sponsored scheme launched in 2007 to increase the production of rice, wheat, pulses, coarse cereals, and oilseeds in India. The mission operates through district level interventions, distributing quality seeds, promoting soil health management, and providing technical support to farmers. It aims to ensure food security by closing the yield gap and enhancing farm productivity in identified districts.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Farmers in districts identified under the mission are eligible
  • Individual farmers and farmer groups can access seed and input assistance
  • Priority for small and marginal farmers and women farmers

Benefits

  • Distribution of certified and hybrid seeds at subsidised rates
  • Assistance for nutrient management and soil amendments
  • Support for farm machinery and water saving devices
  • Technical training and crop demonstration support

How to Apply

  1. Contact the district agriculture office or KVK in your area
  2. Enrol for the mission's input distribution and demonstrations
  3. Receive seeds and technical guidance as per the district plan

Required Documents

  • Land records
  • Aadhaar card and bank account details
meta_title: National Food Security Mission: Higher Crop Production Support
meta_description: NFSM boosts rice, wheat, pulses, and oilseed production with subsidised seeds and technical support. Check eligible districts and how to benefit.

content:
Overview

Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) is a flagship centrally sponsored scheme that provides flexibility to states to plan and implement agriculture and allied sector development programmes according to local needs. Launched in 2007, the scheme aims to achieve a 4 percent annual growth in agriculture by supporting projects in crop husbandry, animal husbandry, fisheries, horticulture, and marketing infrastructure. States prepare annual plans and receive central funding for approved projects.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Farmers and farmer groups benefit through state level projects under the scheme
  • State agriculture departments and allied departments implement the projects
  • Priority sectors include value addition, infrastructure, and technology adoption

Benefits

  • Funding for state specific agricultural development projects
  • Support for farm infrastructure, post-harvest facilities, and marketing
  • Assistance for livestock, fisheries, and horticulture development
  • Encourages convergence of schemes for holistic farm growth

How to Apply

  1. Beneficiary selection happens through state agriculture departments under approved annual plans
  2. Farmers can contact their district agriculture office to be included in project activities
  3. Individual applications follow the state's project implementation guidelines

Required Documents

  • As specified by the implementing state department for each project
meta_title: Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana: State Agriculture Development
meta_description: RKVY funds state-driven agriculture and allied sector projects for farm growth. Learn how states plan projects and how farmers can benefit.

content:
Overview

The Soil Health Card (SHC) scheme is a centrally sponsored programme that provides every farmer with a card containing nutrient status of their soil. Launched in 2015, the scheme tests soil samples every two years for 12 parameters including nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and micronutrients. Based on the test results, the card recommends the right quantity of fertilisers and soil amendments, helping farmers improve productivity while reducing input costs.

Eligibility Criteria

  • All farmers in India are eligible for soil health cards
  • Soil samples are collected from farmer fields through designated centres
  • No registration fee is charged for soil testing

Benefits

  • Free soil testing and a personalised soil health card for every farmer
  • Recommendations for balanced fertiliser use to improve crop yield
  • Reduction in unnecessary fertiliser expenditure and prevention of soil degradation
  • Improved crop quality and long-term soil fertility

How to Apply

  1. Contact your village level worker, agriculture officer, or soil testing laboratory
  2. Provide field details and allow soil sample collection
  3. Receive the soil health card with test results and recommendations
  4. Follow the recommended nutrient plan in the next cropping seasons

Required Documents

  • Farmer identity proof such as Aadhaar
  • Land details
meta_title: Soil Health Card Scheme: Free Soil Testing for Farmers
meta_description: Soil Health Card gives farmers free soil testing every two years with fertiliser recommendations. Learn how to get your soil tested and benefits.

content:
Overview

The Micro Irrigation Fund (MIF) is a dedicated fund set up with NABARD to promote the adoption of micro-irrigation systems such as drip and sprinkler irrigation across India. The fund provides concessional financing to states for expanding micro-irrigation coverage beyond the existing subsidy programmes. It aims to improve water use efficiency, reduce energy consumption in agriculture, and support the target of more crop per drop.

Eligibility Criteria

  • State governments and state agencies can avail funds from the Micro Irrigation Fund
  • Farmers benefit through subsidised drip and sprinkler systems implemented by states
  • Priority for water scarce regions and horticulture belts

Benefits

  • Additional coverage of micro-irrigation beyond normal subsidy ceilings
  • Reduced water consumption and lower pumping costs for farmers
  • Higher yields, especially for horticultural and high value crops
  • Concessional interest rates on funds provided to states

How to Apply

  1. Farmers should approach the district agriculture office for micro-irrigation subsidy under the state's programme
  2. States access MIF resources through NABARD for implementation
  3. Individual farmers receive assistance as per the state's approved guidelines

Required Documents

  • Land records
  • Aadhaar card and bank account details
meta_title: Micro Irrigation Fund: Drip & Sprinkler Subsidy Support
meta_description: The Micro Irrigation Fund with NABARD expands drip and sprinkler irrigation coverage. Learn how states and farmers can benefit from the fund.

content:
Overview

The National Bamboo Mission is a centrally sponsored scheme for the holistic development of the bamboo sector in India. Restructured in 2018, the mission promotes bamboo plantation on non-forest and forest lands, develops value chains, and supports the bamboo processing industry. It focuses on creating livelihood opportunities in bamboo growing regions while meeting the demand for bamboo in construction, furniture, crafts, and biomass applications.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Farmers, farmer producer organisations, and entrepreneurs engaged in bamboo cultivation or processing
  • Groups and institutions with land suitable for bamboo plantation
  • Bamboo artisans and processors can access training and marketing support

Benefits

  • Financial assistance for bamboo plantation establishment and maintenance
  • Support for nursery development, tissue culture, and quality planting material
  • Assistance for bamboo processing units, craft clusters, and value addition
  • Marketing linkages and support for bamboo based enterprises

How to Apply

  1. Contact the state bamboo mission or the horticulture department
  2. Submit plantation or enterprise proposals as per the mission guidelines
  3. Receive assistance after approval and verification of the proposal

Required Documents

  • Land ownership or lease records
  • Aadhaar card and bank account details
  • Project proposal for processing units, if applicable
meta_title: National Bamboo Mission: Plantation & Processing Assistance
meta_description: National Bamboo Mission supports bamboo plantation, nurseries, and processing enterprises. Check eligibility, financial assistance, and how to apply.

content:
Overview

PM Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA) is an umbrella scheme to ensure remunerative prices to farmers for their produce, especially oilseeds, pulses, and copra. The scheme combines the Price Support Scheme (PSS), Price Deficiency Payment Scheme (PDPS), and Private Procurement Stockist Scheme (PPSS) to strengthen the minimum support price (MSP) mechanism. It ensures that farmers receive at least the MSP when market prices fall below it.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Farmers growing notified oilseeds, pulses, and copra crops are eligible
  • Procurement is done at the declared MSP through designated agencies
  • Farmers registered with the state procurement machinery can participate

Benefits

  • Assured MSP for notified crops through direct procurement
  • Price deficiency payments when market prices fall below MSP
  • Private sector participation in procurement to expand reach
  • Direct payment of the support amount to farmers' bank accounts

How to Apply

  1. Register with the nearest procurement centre or state agency when procurement is announced
  2. Bring the produce to the designated collection centre for quality assessment
  3. Receive the MSP payment directly in your bank account

Required Documents

  • Aadhaar card and bank account details
  • Land records
  • Crop details as per the procurement guidelines
meta_title: PM-AASHA: MSP Assurance for Farmers' Produce
meta_description: PM-AASHA guarantees MSP for oilseeds, pulses, and copra through procurement and price deficiency payments. Know eligibility and how it works.

content:
Overview

Gramin Bhandaran Yojana is a capital investment subsidy scheme for the construction and renovation of rural godowns and cold storage facilities. Launched by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, the scheme encourages farmers, cooperatives, and entrepreneurs to create scientific storage capacity in rural areas. It reduces post-harvest losses and allows farmers to store produce and sell at better prices instead of distress selling.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Farmers, agricultural graduates, and cooperative societies can avail the scheme
  • Entrepreneurs and companies setting up rural storage facilities are eligible
  • Storage units can be used for agricultural produce, inputs, and processed products

Benefits

  • Capital subsidy for construction of godowns, typically 25 to 33 percent of the project cost depending on category
  • Reduced post-harvest losses through scientific storage
  • Better price realisation by enabling farmers to store and sell later
  • Eligibility for bank loans for the remaining project cost

How to Apply

  1. Prepare a project proposal with cost estimates for the godown
  2. Apply through the implementing agency, NABARD, or the district agriculture office
  3. Get the project sanctioned and construct the facility as per approved specifications
  4. Claim the subsidy after completion and verification

Required Documents

  • Identity proof and bank account details
  • Land documents for the proposed facility
  • Project cost estimate and quotation
meta_title: Gramin Bhandaran Yojana: Subsidy for Rural Godowns
meta_description: Gramin Bhandaran Yojana offers capital subsidy for rural godown and cold storage construction. Check eligibility, subsidy rates, and application process.

content:
Overview

The Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) is a central sector scheme launched in 2020 with a fund of Rs 1 lakh crore to support farm gate infrastructure in India. The scheme provides medium and long term loans for post-harvest management infrastructure such as warehouses, cold chains, sorting and grading units, and custom hiring centres. Farmers, farmer producer organisations, agri-entrepreneurs, and start-ups can avail loans with interest subvention.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Farmers, farmer producer organisations (FPOs), and self help groups
  • Agri-entrepreneurs, start-ups, and agri-tech companies
  • Primary agricultural credit societies and cooperatives
  • Loans are available for post-harvest infrastructure projects at the farm gate

Benefits

  • Loans up to Rs 2 crore per project through eligible lending institutions
  • Interest subvention of 3 percent per annum on loans up to the limit
  • Credit guarantee coverage for loans up to a specified limit
  • Support for a wide range of infrastructure including warehouses, cold stores, and processing units

How to Apply

  1. Prepare a project proposal for the eligible infrastructure
  2. Apply for a loan through any eligible bank or lending institution
  3. Submit the proposal on the AIF online portal for interest subvention approval
  4. Complete the project and claim the subvention through the portal

Required Documents

  • Identity and address proof
  • Project proposal with cost estimates
  • Bank account and loan documents as per the lending institution
meta_title: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund: Rs 2 Crore Loans for Farmers
meta_description: AIF provides loans up to Rs 2 crore with 3% interest subvention for farm gate infrastructure like warehouses and cold chains. Check eligibility and apply.

content:
Overview

The National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) is one of the missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change. The mission promotes sustainable agricultural practices that adapt to and mitigate climate change, focusing on soil health, water conservation, and climate resilient cropping systems. It supports location specific interventions such as rainfed area development, soil and water conservation, and agro-forestry.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Farmers in rainfed and climate vulnerable regions are the primary beneficiaries
  • Individual farmers and farmer groups can access assistance for soil and water conservation works
  • Priority for small and marginal farmers and tribal areas

Benefits

  • Assistance for soil conservation, rainwater harvesting, and farm ponds
  • Support for organic inputs, green manuring, and agro-forestry
  • Promotion of climate resilient crop varieties and practices
  • Training and awareness for sustainable farming methods

How to Apply

  1. Contact the district agriculture office for NMSA activities in your area
  2. Participate in village level planning for soil and water conservation works
  3. Receive assistance as per the approved district action plan

Required Documents

  • Land records
  • Aadhaar card and bank account details
meta_title: National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture: Climate Smart Farming
meta_description: NMSA promotes climate resilient agriculture with support for soil conservation, water harvesting, and organic inputs. Check eligibility and benefits.

content:
Overview

Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) is the flagship crop insurance scheme of the Government of India, launched in 2016. The scheme provides comprehensive risk coverage for crops against natural calamities, pests, and diseases at a very low premium. Farmers pay a nominal premium of 2 percent of the sum insured for kharif crops, 1.5 percent for rabi crops, and 5 percent for commercial and horticultural crops, with the balance shared by the government.

Eligibility Criteria

  • All farmers growing notified crops in the insured area, including sharecroppers and tenant farmers
  • Loanee farmers are covered compulsorily, while non-loanee farmers can enrol voluntarily
  • Farmers must have insurable interest in the notified crop

Benefits

  • Full sum insured cover for notified crops against yield losses
  • Coverage for prevented sowing, post-harvest losses, and localised calamities
  • Very low premium burden for farmers, with government sharing the balance
  • Timely claim settlement directly to the farmer's bank account

How to Apply

  1. Loanee farmers are auto-enrolled by the lending bank
  2. Non-loanee farmers can enrol through the insurance company, bank, or online portal before the cut-off date
  3. Submit the enrolment form with land and crop details and pay the premium
  4. Report crop losses to the insurance company or through the portal for claim assessment

Required Documents

  • Aadhaar card and bank account details
  • Land records
  • Crop sown details and loan documents, if applicable
meta_title: PM Fasal Bima Yojana: Crop Insurance at 2% Premium
meta_description: PMFBY offers full crop insurance coverage at 2% premium for kharif, 1.5% for rabi, and 5% for horticultural crops. Check eligibility and how to enrol.

content:
Overview

Pradhan Mantri Krishi Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY) is a pension scheme for small and marginal farmers in India, providing a monthly pension of Rs 3,000 after the age of 60. Farmers between 18 and 40 years can enrol by contributing a fixed monthly amount, with the central government making an equal contribution to the pension fund. The scheme gives elderly farmers a steady income and social security after their working years.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Small and marginal farmers owning up to 2 hectares of cultivable land
  • Age between 18 and 40 years at enrolment
  • Not a member of EPFO, ESIC, or NPS and not an income tax payer

Benefits

  • Monthly pension of Rs 3,000 on attaining 60 years of age
  • Equal central government contribution to the pension account
  • Spouse receives 50 percent family pension after the farmer's death
  • Contributions as low as Rs 55 per month for young farmers

How to Apply

  1. Visit a Common Service Centre or the PM-KMY web portal
  2. Fill the enrolment form with land, Aadhaar, and bank details
  3. Submit the form and begin the monthly contribution

Required Documents

  • Aadhaar card and bank account details
  • Land records or self declaration
  • Mobile number linked to Aadhaar
meta_title: PM Krishi Maan-Dhan Yojana: Pension for Small Farmers
meta_description: PM-KMY provides Rs 3,000 monthly pension to small and marginal farmers after age 60 with matching government contribution. Check eligibility and apply.

content:
Overview

RKVY-RAFTAAR, or Remunerative Approaches for Agriculture and Allied Sector Rejuvenation, is the restructured version of the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana. The scheme supports states in planning and implementing projects across agriculture and allied sectors, with an emphasis on value addition, entrepreneurship, and agri-business. It encourages outcome based funding and convergence of schemes to double farm incomes and create rural employment.

Eligibility Criteria

  • State agriculture and allied departments implement projects under the scheme
  • Farmers, farmer producer organisations, and agri-entrepreneurs benefit through state projects
  • Projects in value chains, marketing infrastructure, and technology adoption are prioritised

Benefits

  • Flexible funding for state specific agricultural projects
  • Support for agri-business incubation and value addition
  • Assistance for farm mechanisation and post-harvest infrastructure
  • Promotion of allied sectors such as dairy, fisheries, and horticulture

How to Apply

  1. Project proposals are prepared and submitted by state departments
  2. Farmers can contact the district agriculture office to participate in approved projects
  3. Individual benefit follows the state's implementation guidelines

Required Documents

  • As specified by the implementing state department
meta_title: RKVY-RAFTAAR: Agri-Business & Value Addition Support
meta_description: RKVY-RAFTAAR funds state agriculture projects with focus on value addition, agri-business, and farm mechanisation. Learn how states and farmers benefit.

content:
Overview

Gramin Krishi Mausam Sewa is the agrometeorological advisory service of the India Meteorological Department (IMD). The scheme provides crop and location specific weather advisories to farmers through Agromet Field Units and the network of state agricultural universities. Farmers receive SMS alerts and bulletins on rainfall, temperature, humidity, and pest conditions, helping them plan sowing, irrigation, fertiliser application, and harvesting activities.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Open to all farmers across India; no registration fee for advisories
  • Farmers can subscribe to SMS alerts through the Meghdoot app or with local agriculture offices
  • Agromet Field Units cover block level advisories in partner districts

Benefits

  • Free crop specific weather advisories on mobile phones
  • Timely warnings about adverse weather and pest outbreaks
  • Better planning of farm operations, reducing crop losses
  • Advisories prepared by scientists in collaboration with state agriculture universities

How to Apply

  1. Download the Meghdoot app or register your mobile number through local agriculture offices
  2. Select your crop and location to receive relevant advisories
  3. Follow the weekly advisories for farm operations

Required Documents

  • Mobile number for SMS alerts
  • No other documents are required
meta_title: Gramin Krishi Mausam Sewa: Weather Advisories for Farmers
meta_description: Gramin Krishi Mausam Sewa provides free crop-specific weather advisories to farmers via SMS and the Meghdoot app. Learn how to subscribe.

content:
Overview

The Sub-Mission on Seeds and Planting Material is a component of the National Mission on Agricultural Extension and Technology that strengthens the production and distribution of quality seeds in India. The sub-mission supports seed villages, foundation and certified seed production, seed infrastructure, and quality control laboratories. It ensures farmers get access to improved and certified seeds of high yielding varieties to raise productivity.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Seed growers, farmer groups, and cooperative societies engaged in seed production
  • State seed corporations and private seed companies are supported
  • Farmers can purchase certified seeds at subsidised rates through the distribution network

Benefits

  • Support for seed village programmes and certified seed production
  • Subsidy on quality seeds of pulses, oilseeds, and cereals
  • Assistance for seed processing plants, cold storage, and testing labs
  • Improved access to high yielding and climate resilient varieties

How to Apply

  1. Contact the district agriculture office or state seed corporation for seed availability
  2. Seed producers can apply for assistance under the sub-mission's production programmes
  3. Follow the state's distribution procedure for subsidised seeds

Required Documents

  • Land records for seed production
  • Aadhaar card and bank account details
meta_title: Sub-Mission on Seeds: Quality Seed Production & Subsidy
meta_description: The Sub-Mission on Seeds and Planting Material supports certified seed production and subsidised quality seeds for farmers. Check eligibility and benefits.

content:
Overview

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana Plus, also known as PM-KISAN Plus, is an initiative that extends income support to landless farmers who are members of women self help groups (SHGs) engaged in agriculture and allied activities. Launched as an extension of the PM-KISAN scheme, it provides financial support directly to the bank accounts of eligible women SHG members, complementing the original scheme that covers landholding farmers.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Women members of self help groups engaged in agriculture or allied activities
  • Landless farmers who are not covered under the original PM-KISAN scheme
  • Members must be verified through the SHG network and meet the programme norms

Benefits

  • Direct financial support to the bank accounts of eligible SHG members
  • Income support for landless women farmers engaged in agriculture
  • Strengthens the role of women in farming and allied livelihoods
  • Payments made in instalments as per the programme guidelines

How to Apply

  1. Enrolment is done through the self help group network and the state rural livelihood mission
  2. Eligible members are verified against the programme database
  3. Benefits are transferred directly to the member's bank account

Required Documents

  • Aadhaar card and bank account details
  • SHG membership details
meta_title: PM-KISAN Plus: Support for Landless Women Farmers
meta_description: PM-KISAN Plus extends income support to landless women SHG members engaged in agriculture. Check eligibility, enrolment process, and benefits.
